intro: The simplest way to read and write a device over Ethernet. A device keeps its data in numbered 16-bit registers. A client asks for some registers by number and gets their contents back. Nothing in the protocol says what a register means: that is in the device's manual.

connect.title: Connect
connect.text: The plant controller opens a TCP connection to the inverter on port 502. Modbus TCP has no login and no start command: the connection is enough.

read.title: Read the power
read.text: The manual lists active power at register 40101. On the wire this is address 100, because the wire counts from 0. The answer is 4 bytes: one 32-bit float in two registers, 4820.5 kW.

limit.title: Set a limit
limit.text: The grid operator asks for less power. The controller writes 3000 into address 200, the power limit. The inverter answers with an exact copy of the request: that copy means done.

check.title: Check it worked
check.text: Modbus never reports a change by itself: the client must ask again. Six seconds later the power is 2998.7 kW.

mistake.title: A wrong address
mistake.text: A new script sends the manual's number, 40101, as the address. The inverter has no register there, so it answers with an exception instead of data.

frames.tcp: Open a TCP connection to port 502
frames.write-req: Set the power limit to 3000 kW

notes.tcp: Plain TCP, no Modbus bytes yet. Many devices accept only a few connections at a time, so a client keeps its connection open and reuses it.

tid-1.name: Transaction ID 1
tid-1.note: A number the client picks. The answer carries the same one, so the client can match them.

tid-2.name: Transaction ID 2
tid-2.note: The next request, the next number.

tid-4.name: Transaction ID 4
tid-4.note: Even an error answer carries the request's number.

len-6.name: Length
len-6.note: 6 bytes follow: the unit ID and 5 bytes of request.

unit.name: Unit ID 1
unit.note: Picks a device behind a gateway. This inverter answers to 1.

fc06-echo.name: Function 06
fc06-echo.note: The answer to a write repeats the request byte for byte.

fc83.name: Function 83
fc83.note: 0x83 = 0x03 + 0x80. The highest bit set means: this is an error.

addr-40101.name: Address 40101
addr-40101.note: 0x9CA5 = 40101: the manual's number, sent as it is. Wrong: the inverter has nothing there.

reg-100.name: Register 100
reg-100.note: 0xA400: the low half of the float. This inverter sends the low word first (CDAB).

reg-101.name: Register 101
reg-101.note: 0x4596: the high half. High then low, 0x4596A400, is 4820.5 (kW).

code-02.name: Exception 02
code-02.note: Illegal data address: the register does not exist. 01 would mean an unknown function, 03 a bad value.

a-table.name: Table
a-table.note: 4: a holding register, read with function 03. 3 is an input register (function 04), 1 a discrete input, 0 a coil.

a-number.name: Number
a-number.note: 0101: the 101st register. Manuals count from 1, the wire counts from 0.

facts.standard: Modbus Application Protocol V1.1b3 and Modbus Messaging on TCP/IP V1.0b (Modbus Organization)
facts.between: Client (plant controller, SCADA, logger) → server (inverter, meter, battery)
facts.security: None. Anyone who reaches port 502 can read and write. Modbus/TCP Security adds TLS on port 802.
facts.frames: A 7-byte MBAP header, then a function code and its data
facts.since: 1979 on serial lines (Modicon), on TCP since 1999

tips: Find out whether the manual counts registers from 0 or from 1. One register off reads half of one value and half of the next, and that can look almost right.
Check the word order of 32-bit values against a value you know, such as the power on the inverter's display. Many devices send the low word first (CDAB).
Many devices accept only a few TCP connections. A test tool left connected can lock out the plant controller.
Modbus has no passwords. Keep port 502 inside the plant network, and never let it be reached from the internet.

anatomy.register: A register number from a manual, and the address that goes on the wire

playground.encoder: This inverter sends a 32-bit float low word first (CDAB). Type a value to see its bytes, and what the same bytes mean when read in another order.
playground.file: The inverter's register map, from its manual. The controller must be set up with the same addresses, types and word order.
playground.unit: The unit ID the inverter answers to.
playground.offset: How to turn a register number into an address. Look for this in every manual: some count from 0.
playground.float: Two registers, one float, low word first. The controller must be set to CDAB.
playground.scaled: An integer with a scale: 5001 means 50.01 Hz.
playground.uint32: Also two registers, also low word first.
playground.limit: Writable: the limit the controller sets in step 3.
playground.fallback: If the controller stops writing for this long, the inverter goes back to its fallback setting. A lost link then does not leave the plant stuck at an old limit.
